A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EnergyMoGen and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite appendix expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation experiments on HumanML3D, KIT-ML and MTT, CompML augmentation results, and component and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds inference-time measurements, foot-contact scores and a qualitative failure example.

M1.justification: The motion VAE, cross-attention denoiser, adaptive gradient descent, latent-aware and semantic-aware composition, and Synergistic Energy Fusion remain unchanged. The skeleton-based temporal composition procedure is also retained.

E1.justification: Appendix J/Figure 8 adds a qualitative scenario described as involving a completely novel concept: playing table tennis. HumanML3D, KIT-ML, MTT, CompML and the established tasks remain unchanged; no systematic novel-concept test set is introduced.

E2.justification: The new inference-time comparison in Table 10 evaluates EnergyMoGen against FineMoGen, MLD and GUESS. These methods already appeared in accuracy comparisons, whose comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds average inference time per sentence and Physical Foot Contact evaluation on MTT (Tables 10–11). Existing splits, training budgets and sampling settings are retained. The printed FID formula is revised, without establishing an implementation change or experimental rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices F–G add inference-cost and foot-sliding analyses, including a direct comparison of fusion against individual generation variants. Appendix J adds a failure case. Existing ablations remain unchanged; new Figure 6 visualizes results already reported in Table 7.

E5.justification: The existing reporting of 20 evaluations and 95% confidence intervals is retained. The new timing and foot-contact tables add point estimates without new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain identical values. New Table 10 reports inference times of 0.66 seconds for EnergyMoGen, 2.54 for FineMoGen, 0.21 for MLD and 1.79 for GUESS. Table 11 adds PFC scores of 0.61, 0.54, 1.05 and 0.51 for multi-concept, latent-only, semantic-only and SEF generation, respectively. Figure 8 adds a failure outcome.

T1.justification: Equation 12 changes the printed FID definition by replacing the covariance-product term with its square root. The energy-based, diffusion and composition derivations are otherwise retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The new contribution summary explicitly claims the first attempt to solve motion composition from an energy perspective. v1 presents the approach without this explicit priority claim. The abstract, main performance claims and CompML contribution remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix J newly acknowledges difficulty with completely novel concepts and links this limitation to the table-tennis failure example. Appendix G interprets the new foot-contact results as supporting SEF's effectiveness. Existing mechanism interpretations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix A retain the architecture sizes, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, training iterations and inference settings. The project access information is unchanged. The new timing results do not provide additional hardware or measurement implementation details.

R1.justification: v2 adds four references covering Hopfield memory capacity, latent diffusion transformer theory, energy-based navigation and EDGE, which supplies the PFC metric. It also adds explicit first-attempt positioning. The main related-work discussion remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the introduction's discussion of latent-to-motion correspondence, adds a contribution summary and acknowledgments, and makes localized language edits. New appendix sections expand the organization, while the main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–11, a two-panel visualization of existing ablation results as Figure 6, and the failure illustration as Figure 8. The previous energy-distribution Figure 6 becomes Figure 7. Existing tables and visual examples are preserved, with localized layout changes.

improvement.justification: The new foot-contact comparison strengthens evidence for SEF's claimed reduction in foot sliding. Timing results and the explicit novel-concept failure case clarify practical tradeoffs and limitations. These are useful but limited gains over unchanged methods and benchmark results; the timing comparison remains underspecified regarding hardware and measurement conditions.
